Leading the Toronto Metropolitan Neurotech team in researching and exploring various methodologies and applications of BCI technology, electroencephalography (EEG), and neurofeedback to improve modern practices. Toronto Metropolitan Neurotech (TMNT) is one of the university's newest student engineering groups. TMNT focuses on the instersection of EEG signal processing and closed-loop neurofeedback systems with the goal of building technology that reads brain activity and uses it to adaptively modify sensory input stimuli in real time.

Current proposals under consideration include: intraoperative brain stimulation (with VR/AR integration), phantom pain treatment, gifted student assessment, and chronic pain diagnosis. All of which are built on the same core architecture
